2_Introduction: The PCE for the device reached 14.392%, with a JSC of 18.961 mA/cm², a VOC of 1.0127 V and a FF of 74.955%. The perovskite (Cs0.1FA0.9Pb1I2.8Br0.2) solution was prepared with a concentration of 1.6 mol/L in mixed solvent of DMF and DMSO. Then the filtered perovskite precursor was spin-coated on the substrate at 1000 rpm for 10 s and 5000 rpm for 30 s. During the second spin coating step, 120 µL CB was dripped onto the perovskite film at 10 s before ending the program. The substrates were immediately transferred to the hotplate and annealed at 110 °C for 15 min. Image analysis shows that the spin-coating coverage reaches 98.8%, and the average grayscale value of the film is 10.6284.
3_Result_Discussion: The high-performance perovskite solar cell arises from a tightly coupled interplay between compositional design, kinetic crystallization control, and interfacial defect engineering—though no explicit SAMs, additives, or passivators are introduced in the protocol, the intrinsic stability and optoelectronic quality of the Cs₀.₁FA₀.₉PbI₂.₈Br₀.₂ absorber are critically governed by its A-site cation alloying (enhancing Goldschmidt tolerance factor to ~0.93 and suppressing δ-phase formation), B/X-site stoichiometry (minimizing PbI₂ residuals and halide vacancy density), and precisely tuned crystallization dynamics: the 1.6 mol/L precursor concentration ensures sufficient nucleation density without excessive supersaturation, while the two-step spin-coating (1000 rpm/10 s for wet-film formation followed by 5000 rpm/30 s for rapid solvent extraction) synergizes with the timed antisolvent quench (120 µL chlorobenzene at 10 s into the high-speed step) to arrest intermediate solvate phases and promote homogeneous nucleation across the substrate, thereby suppressing pinholes and grain-boundary traps; subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C for 15 min drives complete ligand dissociation, crystal coalescence, and strain relaxation, as corroborated by the image-derived film coverage of 98.8% and low average grayscale value of 10.6284—quantitative optical indicators of exceptional morphological uniformity, minimal void fraction, and nanoscale continuity that collectively suppress shunt pathways and spatially homogenize non-radiative recombination; this near-perfect film morphology directly underpins extended carrier diffusion lengths and reduced trap-assisted recombination, enabling simultaneous optimization of open-circuit voltage, short-circuit current density, fill factor, and power conversion efficiency to 1.0127 V, 18.961 mA/cm², 74.955%, and 14.392%, respectively.
